globalRules.description: Any default of 1 for installed or replaced quantity is only a visible conservative placeholder, never source-backed truth.
globalRules.implementationNotes: When no quote, invoice, audit, worksheet, or user-entered value is present, prefill 1 only in the UI as editable placeholder/test-case data. Mark estimate confidence low until the user confirms the quantity or RetroFi derives it from a quote/invoice.

globalRules.description: Normalize raw quantity aliases, camelCase variants, and measure-specific count fields into canonical quantity inputs by retrofit family.
globalRules.implementationNotes: Treat unit_count, unitcount, quantity, equipment_quantity, measure_quantity, eligible_quantity, eligible_unit_count, number_of_units, device_count, system_count, installation_count, and similar fields as installed/replaced unit quantities unless the raw key explicitly refers to an account number, cost, efficiency rating, energy savings, capacity, square feet, linear feet, tons, kW, kWh, therms, gallons, or horsepower.

globalRules.description: Fields that combine count with capacity or area must not be silently mapped to unit_count.
globalRules.implementationNotes: For raw keys such as unit_count_or_tons, tons_or_unit_count, quantity_or_size, capacity_or_unit_count, unit_count_or_square_feet, quantity_or_equipment_size, size_or_savings, and tons_or_horsepower_or_square_feet_or_linear_feet_as_applicable, expose a required dimension selector in the UI and store the numeric value in the selected canonical field. Do not infer the unit from the number alone.

globalRules.description: Use retrofit-family-specific UI labels for quantity fields so users understand what is being counted.
globalRules.implementationNotes: Examples: lighting uses Number of fixtures or lamps to replace; EV charging uses Number of charger ports or stations; windows/doors uses Number of windows or doors; HVAC uses Number of systems or units; controls uses Number of thermostats, zone sensors, or controlled fans.

globalRules.description: Installed/replaced count fields should be non-negative integers with no artificially small maximum.
globalRules.implementationNotes: Use integer validation with min 0. A soft warning may flag unusually large values for review, but the system must allow large commercial projects such as 1000+ bulbs, fixtures, ports, devices, windows, or motors.

globalRules.description: Raw keys containing account, member_account, residential_account, commercial_account, utility_account, or customer_account are eligibility/profile identifiers, not quantities.
globalRules.implementationNotes: Do not include account identifiers in retrofitQuantityOverrides. Store as strings to preserve leading zeros and formatting, even if observed value type is number.

globalRules.description: Equipment, charger, thermostat, measure, project, report, and eligible cost fields should map to quote/project cost inputs, not scope quantities.
globalRules.implementationNotes: Parse observed numeric dollars into currency_cents where possible. Prefer quote or invoice. If only a user estimate is available, mark confidence medium or low depending on source.

globalRules.description: Annual kWh, therm, kW reduction, and custom savings fields materially affect dollar estimates and should come from verified savings, program worksheet, utility data, or explicit user estimate.
globalRules.implementationNotes: Prefer verified or approved fields over estimated/user-entered values. For custom projects, do not synthesize savings from unit_count unless a retrofit model explicitly supports the selected measure.

globalRules.description: Normalize aliases by lowercasing, removing punctuation and separators, splitting camelCase, expanding common abbreviations, and treating singular/plural forms as equivalent.
globalRules.implementationNotes: Examples: installedCost, installed_cost, installedcost, installed project cost, and installed_project_cost should resolve through the same alias layer before field-specific disambiguation. Source prompt:

globalRules.description: Represent monetary values in canonical *_cents fields. Raw numeric dollar fields should be multiplied by 100 when the observed label lacks a cents suffix; raw cents fields should pass through without scaling.
globalRules.implementationNotes: When a raw value is text, parse only unambiguous currency strings. If the string includes ranges, conditions, or program language, preserve it as a document or admin-review value rather than silently coercing.

globalRules.description: For dollars that materially affect the estimate, use itemized quote, invoice, receipt, or explicit user input before any placeholder. Do not hide assumed project costs.
globalRules.implementationNotes: If both a quote and invoice are present, use the quote for preapproval estimates and the paid invoice for final claim estimates unless program rules state otherwise.

globalRules.description: Any raw field that means number of installed, replaced, purchased, controlled, connected, or eligible units must map to unit_count or a retrofit-family-specific quantity field. A default of 1 is only a visible placeholder and must reduce confidence until confirmed.
globalRules.implementationNotes: Do not treat placeholder quantity 1 as source-backed. Labels should adapt by retrofit family, such as number of fixtures, charger ports, windows, thermostats, motors, HVAC units, linear feet, square feet, tons, kW, controlled watts, or other program units.

globalRules.description: Current rate tables, tariff credits, rate schedules, and published program rates are time-sensitive and must be sourced from current official program or utility tariff sources at runtime, not from stale package defaults.
globalRules.implementationNotes: If current source-backed rate data is unavailable, set calculation status to program_source_repair_required or admin_review instead of inventing a rate.

globalRules.description: Canonical date fields must use ISO 8601 dates. Text dates, combined date fields, and relative timing attestations should be parsed only when unambiguous.
globalRules.implementationNotes: Fields such as purchase_or_installation_date and invoice_and_installation_date should populate the specific dates only when separable; otherwise retain source_documentation_status or timing_attestation.

globalRules.description: Inputs that require program administrator determination, award selection, approved savings, approved baseline, approved incentive, verified savings, or current official table lookup should not be shown as ordinary applicant-entered facts.
globalRules.implementationNotes: Expose applicant-facing upload or attestation steps where useful, but final values should be admin_review or program_source_repair_required.

globalRules.description: Any value used only to make test cases calculable must be explicitly synthetic and overrideable, with low default confidence when it can materially change dollars.
globalRules.implementationNotes: Synthetic defaults are appropriate for QA fixtures, not user-facing final estimates.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize casing, punctuation, spaces, and camelCase variants. Use selected_measure over generic measure_type when both are present. Match normalized value to the current program measure table when available; otherwise keep as free text and require program source repair or admin review before final calculation.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Incorrect measure selection can apply the wrong rebate row, rate, eligibility rule, or cap.
inputMappings.notes: This is the primary measure classifier and should drive which quantity label and dimension inputs are displayed.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Store scope text as entered. If approved_* scope is present, retain it as program-approved scope and use it over user-entered project_scope for final estimates. Use custom_project_scope to trigger custom savings workflow.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Scope mismatch can cause RetroFi to estimate an ineligible or partially eligible project.
inputMappings.notes: Scope fields should supplement, not replace, structured measure and quantity fields.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize project-type aliases. Use program-specific enum mapping when source rules distinguish retrofit, new construction, direct install, custom, prescriptive, audit, replacement, or conversion.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Project type often changes eligible rates, cost caps, and preapproval requirements.
inputMappings.notes: Do not collapse project_type into measure_selection; it is a program-calculation modifier.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Number of units to install or replace
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use quote/invoice quantity, measure table worksheet quantity, or explicit user input when present. Otherwise prefill 1 as visible editable placeholder. If a measure-specific count exists, prefer the more specific canonical field, such as port_count, fixture_count, thermostat_count, or steam_trap_count, and mirror it to unit_count only for generic per-unit calculations.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: A hidden value of 1 can understate or overstate incentives by orders of magnitude for lighting, EV charging, HVAC, windows, doors, motors, controls, and commercial measures.
inputMappings.notes: This is the default canonical count for raw keys that clearly mean installed/replaced units but do not identify a more specific count dimension.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use explicit port count where available. If only charger_count is present, treat it as station count unless program language pays per port; expose station-vs-port clarification. If minimum_two_ports is affirmative and port_count is missing, set validation warning requiring at least 2 but do not auto-fill 2 as source-backed truth.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: EV incentives may pay per port, per station, or per charger; using 1 silently can materially undercount multi-port or fleet installations.
inputMappings.notes: For EV charging, port_count should be displayed before generic unit_count.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize Level II, L2, Level 2, Wi-Fi enabled, standard, hardwired, outlet, and DCFC terms. If qualified_level_2_charger is yes/true, set charger_type to level_2 unless a more specific charger_type is supplied.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Wrong charger type can select the wrong rebate amount or make an ineligible charger appear eligible.
inputMappings.notes: Keep charger_type separate from port_count and charger_power_kw.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse kW values from numeric or text fields. Use charger model or quote specifications to derive power when available. Do not use charger level alone to infer a specific kW for final estimate unless the program table only requires level classification.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Power rating may affect eligibility tiers, DCFC amounts, load-management requirements, and demand impacts.
inputMappings.notes: For DCFC, require explicit kW or model-derived kW before final estimate.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Store charger model from quote, invoice, application, or user entry. Use model lookup only where RetroFi has a maintained qualified-products table.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: An ineligible model can incorrectly pass eligibility screening.
inputMappings.notes: Model number should be paired with charger_type and charger_power_kw when available.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize free-text equipment categories to RetroFi measure taxonomy. Use proposed_equipment for new equipment and existing_equipment/baseline_equipment for baseline fields.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Wrong equipment type can trigger the wrong measure family, UI quantity label, eligibility filter, and rate table.
inputMappings.notes: Use equipment_type to choose the retrofit family and prompt for family-specific quantity overrides.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Store the existing equipment type separately from proposed equipment. For fuel-switching or replacement measures, combine with existing_fuel and replacement_fuel to determine eligibility.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Baseline misclassification can incorrectly calculate fuel-switching eligibility or savings.
inputMappings.notes: Do not overwrite proposed equipment fields with baseline fields.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize tier labels such as standard, high efficiency, ENERGY STAR, CEE tier, qualified, Wi-Fi, smart, or program-specific tier. Prefer derivation from explicit efficiency ratings or qualified model lists where available.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Efficiency tier can change both eligibility and per-unit incentive amount.
inputMappings.notes: Treat numeric thermostat_tier as a tier code, not a count.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Capture free-text efficiency documentation. If structured ratings such as SEER2, HSPF2, AFUE, EER, or ENERGY STAR flags are present, store them in their dedicated canonical fields and also summarize into equipment_efficiency.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Qualification errors can create false positives for rebates requiring specific efficiency thresholds or qualified product lists.
inputMappings.notes: Final estimates should prefer structured rating fields over unparsed text.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Store full equipment specs text. Parse embedded capacity, model, serial number, efficiency ratings, gallons, tons, kW, horsepower, square feet, and linear feet into dedicated fields when unambiguous.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Specs may contain the decisive eligibility value; unparsed or wrong specs can select the wrong rate table.
inputMappings.notes: Use this as a source field, not a replacement for structured numeric dimensions.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Store model number and serial number from quote, invoice, or application. If model and serial are separately supplied later, split into equipment_model and equipment_serial_number.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Incorrect model can fail product-list eligibility or derive wrong capacity/efficiency.
inputMappings.notes: Serial number is generally post-install verification, while model number can support pre-estimate eligibility.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse numeric tonnage from text or number. Use heat_pump_tons for heat pump capacity and cooling_tons for cooling capacity when measure context requires it. Do not use tons as unit_count.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Many HVAC incentives are paid per ton or have tonnage thresholds; wrong capacity changes estimate materially.
inputMappings.notes: For programs using both unit count and tons, collect both separately.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse BTU/h from text. When unambiguous, derive capacity_tons as BTU/h divided by 12000 and mark derived confidence medium unless confirmed from equipment specs.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: BTU-to-ton conversion errors can apply incorrect HVAC incentive tiers.
inputMappings.notes: Keep original BTU value for auditability.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Require user or program mapping to select dimension: unit_count, eligible_unit_count, capacity_tons, or heating_capacity_tons. Route numeric value to selected canonical input. If unresolved, block reliable final estimate.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: A value of 5 could mean 5 units or 5 tons, producing a materially different incentive.
inputMappings.notes: Do not coerce this field into a plain number without a dimension.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Map area fields to square_feet, preserving subtype metadata such as building, conditioned, insulation, insulated, eligible, or window area. Prefer eligible_square_feet or quote/audit area over gross building area when calculating incentive.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Area-based rebates and caps can scale directly with square footage.
inputMappings.notes: Area is a quantity dimension but not an integer unit_count.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use window area from quote, invoice, or user entry. If window_count also exists, keep both; some programs pay by window while others pay by square foot.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Window incentives may scale by area; using count instead of area can misestimate awards.
inputMappings.notes: Do not infer window_count from square feet unless quote line items provide both.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use eligible_linear_feet over generic linear_feet for incentive calculations. Preserve measure context, such as refrigeration controls, pipe insulation, or case doors.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Linear-foot measures multiply directly by length.
inputMappings.notes: Linear feet is a quantity dimension, not unit_count.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse horsepower from numeric or text fields. Prefer eligible_motor_horsepower or eligible_horsepower for incentive calculations where present.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Motor and refrigeration incentives can be paid per horsepower or restricted by horsepower ranges.
inputMappings.notes: If a measure also has motor count, collect unit_count separately.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: For cow_count_or_horsepower, require dimension selection between cow_count and horsepower. Do not infer from magnitude alone.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Agricultural measures may calculate incentives using herd size or horsepower; confusing them produces invalid estimates.
inputMappings.notes: This is not retrofit unit_count unless the program explicitly pays per cow.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Require dimension selection before calculation. Supported dimensions include unit_count, square_feet, linear_feet, capacity_tons, horsepower, kW, kWh, gallons, or other program-defined size dimension.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Ambiguous numeric values can be interpreted as count, area, capacity, or savings, causing large estimate errors.
inputMappings.notes: This object should unblock legacy inputs while forcing explicit unit resolution.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Number of lighting fixtures or lamps
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use quote/invoice line-item quantity or user input. If generic unit_count appears in a lighting measure, display as fixture_count with lighting-specific label.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Lighting projects can include one fixture or thousands; a hidden default of 1 is especially risky.
inputMappings.notes: Allow large integer values and do not cap at residential-scale quantities.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize LED lamp, fixture, tube, troffer, exterior, interior, controls, and retrofit-kit descriptions to lighting measure taxonomy.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Lighting fixture type determines eligibility, per-unit rates, and required wattage/savings documentation.
inputMappings.notes: Pair with fixture_count and annual_kwh_savings where applicable.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Number of thermostats or zone sensors
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Map count-like thermostat fields to thermostat_count. If qualifying_smart_thermostat or eligible_smart_thermostat is numeric, treat it as count; if boolean-like, treat it as thermostat_eligibility_flag and require count separately.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Smart thermostat and zone sensor rebates are often per device.
inputMappings.notes: Do not confuse thermostat_tier with thermostat_count.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse numeric 1/0, yes/no, true/false into boolean enrollment. Preserve program subtype metadata, such as thermostat program or EV charging rate.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Enrollment may be an eligibility condition rather than a quantity.
inputMappings.notes: Do not map enrollment fields to count even if observed type is number.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Number of HVAC systems or units
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use quote or user-entered system count. For furnace_count, use furnace-specific label. For outdoor_unit_count, store outdoor_unit_count as subtype metadata and do not assume it equals indoor_head_count.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: HVAC incentives may pay per system, per outdoor unit, per furnace, or per ton.
inputMappings.notes: Collect capacity_tons separately whenever HVAC rates are tonnage-based.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use explicit indoor head count for ductless or multi-split systems. Do not infer from system_count unless quote line items show one-to-one mapping.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Some programs distinguish system count, outdoor unit count, indoor head count, and tonnage.
inputMappings.notes: Keep separately from system_count and outdoor_unit_count.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize common heat pump descriptions. If geothermal_status is affirmative, map to geothermal unless a more specific ground-source type is supplied.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Heat pump type drives program eligibility, rate tiers, and required efficiency metrics.
inputMappings.notes: Pair with SEER2, HSPF2, capacity_tons, and existing_heating_fuel where applicable.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse numeric or text status into boolean. When true, set heat_pump_type candidate to geothermal but allow user override.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Geothermal programs and tonnage rules can differ substantially from air-source heat pump rules.
inputMappings.notes: Observed numeric type likely represents boolean/status, not count.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse numeric SEER2 or SEER values from text. Preserve original metric label; do not convert SEER to SEER2 unless RetroFi has an approved conversion model.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Efficiency threshold errors can incorrectly approve or deny HVAC incentives.
inputMappings.notes: Canonical key is seer2 because current programs often use SEER2, but original metric must be stored.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse numeric HSPF2 or HSPF values from text. Preserve original metric label; do not convert HSPF to HSPF2 unless RetroFi has an approved conversion model.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Heating efficiency thresholds can change eligibility and rebate tiers.
inputMappings.notes: Pair with heat_pump_type and capacity_tons.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse numeric EER value from text or number. Use only for measures whose source rules reference EER.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: EER can determine HVAC eligibility or tier.
inputMappings.notes: Do not substitute EER for SEER2/HSPF2.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse AFUE percentage from text such as 95%, 0.95, or 95 AFUE. Normalize to percent points. For furnace_afue, preserve furnace-specific context.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: AFUE thresholds may determine furnace or boiler rebate eligibility.
inputMappings.notes: Do not confuse AFUE with equipment tier text.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize utility and heating fuel terms. When generic fuel_type is present, infer whether it describes existing or replacement fuel from measure context; if unresolved, ask user to classify.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Fuel type affects fuel-switching eligibility, gas/electric savings, and applicable program source.
inputMappings.notes: Prefer existing_heating_fuel over generic fuel_type for replacement projects.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize replacement fuel terms and compare with existing_fuel_type for conversion/fuel-switching measures.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Fuel-switching incentives can be invalid if replacement fuel is misclassified.
inputMappings.notes: Only use this for proposed/replacement equipment.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse yes/no, true/false, or numeric status into boolean. Pair with backup_heat_type and replacement_fuel_type for heat pump programs.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Dual-fuel status can affect heat pump eligibility and incentive tier.
inputMappings.notes: Observed status fields are not count fields.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse gallons from text or number. Use equipment model or quote specs where available. Do not treat gallons as unit_count.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Some water heater programs require minimum tank size or use size to validate product category.
inputMappings.notes: Collect unit_count separately if multiple water heaters are installed.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use quote/invoice line-item quantity or user input. If generic unit_count appears in a windows/doors measure and the selected measure is a door measure, display as door_count.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Door rebates may be per door; projects commonly include multiple doors.
inputMappings.notes: Keep separate from window_count and window_square_feet.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Map explicit window-count aliases when observed or derived from quote line items. If only window_square_feet is supplied, do not infer window_count.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Window rebates may pay per window, per square foot, or both; defaulting to 1 can severely understate incentives.
inputMappings.notes: This canonical field is included even when raw target list only has window_square_feet because the UI needs a window quantity override.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use audit, survey, quote, or user-entered trap count. Apply only for steam trap measures; otherwise leave generic unit_count unaffected.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Steam trap rebates are often per qualifying trap; large commercial sites can have many traps.
inputMappings.notes: Include trap_count as a global alias even though it appears in sample contexts rather than target list.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use explicit fan count for control retrofit measures. If control measure uses kW instead, collect connected_control_kw separately.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Controls incentives may be per fan or per connected kW; wrong dimension changes estimate.
inputMappings.notes: Requires measure context to choose count versus kW.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize lighting controls, fan controls, HVAC controls, occupancy sensors, networked thermostats, and other control retrofit types.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Control type can determine eligible quantity basis and incentive rate.
inputMappings.notes: Pair with controlled_fan_count, thermostat_count, fixture_count, or connected_control_kw as applicable.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse battery kWh from quote, model specs, or user entry. Do not treat kWh capacity as annual energy savings.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Storage incentives often require minimum capacity or pay by kWh capacity.
inputMappings.notes: If multiple batteries are installed, collect eligible_battery_count separately.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use explicit eligible battery count. Preserve qualifier over_10_kwh as validation metadata requiring battery_capacity_kwh >= 10 for each counted unit if program requires it.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Battery count and capacity can both affect storage incentives.
inputMappings.notes: Do not infer count from total battery_capacity_kwh without model/quote line items.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Store battery chemistry/product category and map to qualified-product lists where available.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Battery type may affect eligibility and interconnection requirements.
inputMappings.notes: Pair with model and capacity.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use verified_annual_kwh_savings or approved_annual_kwh_savings when present. Otherwise use estimated/user-entered savings only as low-confidence input. For custom projects, require savings source documentation before reliable final estimate.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Custom incentives may multiply directly by annual kWh savings.
inputMappings.notes: Do not confuse battery kWh or EV charging kWh consumption with savings.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Prefer approved_annual_kwh_savings, verified_annual_kwh_savings, then verified_kwh_savings, then first_year_kwh_savings. Store source provenance and whether value is annual, first-year, deemed, modeled, or measured.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Verified savings often drives custom incentive dollars and caps.
inputMappings.notes: If user overrides verified savings, downgrade confidence unless supported by documentation.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use verified_annual_therm_savings when present. Otherwise treat estimated values as low-confidence until supported by audit, worksheet, or utility data.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Gas custom incentives may multiply by therm savings.
inputMappings.notes: Keep separate from kWh savings and fuel type.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use verified or approved therm savings from program worksheet, audit, utility data, or custom project documentation.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Verified gas savings can be the direct incentive basis for custom measures.
inputMappings.notes: If only estimated_therm_savings exists, map to annual_therm_savings instead.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse kW reduction from verified worksheet, interval data, or user estimate. Do not confuse with charger_power_kw, connected_control_kw, or equipment capacity.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Demand incentives may pay per kW reduced.
inputMappings.notes: Require source provenance for reliable estimates.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use utility bill or interval data when available. Do not treat annual usage as savings.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Annual usage may affect eligibility or savings reasonableness checks.
inputMappings.notes: Store separately from annual_kwh_savings.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use EV charging meter, managed charging platform, user estimate, or utility interval data. Preserve period metadata if not annual.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: EV charging energy may affect managed charging or rate-based incentives, but is not a charger quantity.
inputMappings.notes: Do not map to annual_kwh_savings.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse numeric hours from text. Use operating schedule, audit, or business hours for higher confidence. Do not derive savings without measure model support.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Operating hours can materially affect deemed or custom energy savings.
inputMappings.notes: Relevant for lighting, motors, refrigeration, HVAC controls, and custom measures.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse measure life from source table if present. Prefer program/deemed savings source over user input for final calculations.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Measure life may affect lifecycle benefits, cost-effectiveness, or program-specific caps.
inputMappings.notes: Usually not required for one-time rebate estimates unless source formula uses lifecycle savings.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize residential, commercial, industrial, agricultural, multifamily, nonprofit, public, small business, facility, dwelling, and home-type descriptors. Preserve raw subtype metadata.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Customer/site type can determine eligibility, caps, measure lists, and application pathway.
inputMappings.notes: This is profile context, not retrofit quantity.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Store text description. If numeric square footage can be parsed unambiguously, populate square_feet or building_square_feet subtype metadata.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Size may affect eligibility or savings reasonableness; text alone is not reliable for area-based calculations.
inputMappings.notes: Prefer square_feet for calculations.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use explicit dwelling unit count for multifamily or residential eligibility and caps. Do not treat as installed equipment count unless program explicitly pays per dwelling unit.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Dwelling unit count can affect multifamily eligibility, caps, and per-home limits.
inputMappings.notes: Validation is integer min 0 but default should not be silently 1 unless used only as test data.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize passenger EV, fleet vehicle, school bus, medium-duty, heavy-duty, plug-in hybrid, and other vehicle types where EV charging eligibility references vehicle class.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Some EV charging programs restrict eligible vehicles or customer classes.
inputMappings.notes: Keep separate from qualifying_vehicle_count.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use explicit vehicle count for fleet or managed charging eligibility. Do not substitute for port_count unless source formula pays by enrolled vehicle.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Vehicle count may affect eligibility and enrollment but is not necessarily charger quantity.
inputMappings.notes: For EV charger hardware incentives, port_count remains the primary quantity.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize inspection completed, required, pending, permit signoff, blower door test, and documentation terms. Use boolean only if source field is clearly yes/no.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Inspection and documentation can be required for eligibility or final payment.
inputMappings.notes: This is a timing/compliance field, not a quantity.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Store portal result text and map to statuses such as preapproved, reserved, waitlisted, denied, submitted, or approved where possible.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Portal status can affect whether an incentive remains available or requires preapproval.
inputMappings.notes: Not a measure quantity despite being in the quantity alias list.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse numeric 1/0, yes/no, true/false into eligibility status. Use runtime account verification when available.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Account eligibility can gate program access.
inputMappings.notes: Not a unit count.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Store account identifiers as strings, preserving leading zeros and utility-specific formatting. Do not perform arithmetic. Use only for eligibility/rate/account verification.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Wrong account identifier can check the wrong utility membership, service territory, or rate eligibility.
inputMappings.notes: Observed numeric account fields are identifiers, not quantities.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse numeric or text status into a commercial-account eligibility flag where the program requires commercial service.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Incorrect account class can cause ineligible program matching.
inputMappings.notes: Not a count.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize operating company names from account lookup, service territory, or user selection. Use for jurisdiction-specific program selection.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Operating company can determine rates, forms, and eligible incentive program.
inputMappings.notes: Treat as organization/profile context.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Prefer geocoded address or official program territory lookup. Parse explicit yes/no user entry only as provisional if runtime lookup is unavailable.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Community status can affect eligibility adders, caps, or funding pools.
inputMappings.notes: Not a quantity field.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Map program-specific income bands into RetroFi income tier taxonomy. Require source documentation if program requires verified income eligibility.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Income tier can change rebate amount or eligibility.
inputMappings.notes: Profile field, not scope quantity.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize connected charger, utility-managed charging, time-window compliance, off-peak rate, and charging schedule terms. Use boolean subfields where the program source has yes/no requirements.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Managed charging or off-peak compliance may be required for EV charger incentives.
inputMappings.notes: Compliance is separate from charger_count, port_count, and charger_type.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Map dollar-denominated numeric cost fields to *_cost_cents. If field already ends in _cents, treat as cents. Map counterfactual_interest_rate to financing assumptions, not cost. Prefer quote or invoice over user estimate.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Cost fields affect reimbursement caps, percent-of-cost limits, and financing comparisons.
inputMappings.notes: Included here because several cost-like fields were listed in quantity alias candidates but must not be treated as quantities.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Store assembly or envelope component type and map to weatherization, windows/doors, insulation, or glazing measure taxonomy as applicable.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Assembly type may determine area-based rates and eligibility.
inputMappings.notes: Pair with square_feet, window_square_feet, or door/window count depending on measure.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use conditioned area for HVAC/weatherization sizing, eligibility, or savings reasonableness checks. Do not substitute for eligible measure square feet unless source formula explicitly uses conditioned area.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Conditioned area can affect sizing, eligibility, or savings estimates.
inputMappings.notes: Also mirror into square_feet subtype metadata for general area display.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: When these fields are text or boolean-like, parse as eligibility flags. When numeric and used in a context that clearly means quantity, route to the specific count field such as port_count or thermostat_count.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Qualification fields can be confused with quantities; this can either multiply incentives incorrectly or ignore device counts.
inputMappings.notes: Disambiguate based on value type and label: yes/no means flag; integer count means quantity.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Require explicit selection among capacity_tons, horsepower, square_feet, linear_feet, charger_power_kw, annual_kwh_savings, annual_therm_savings, kw_reduction, or another program-defined dimension.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Size and savings fields are not interchangeable and can drive different formulas.
inputMappings.notes: Block reliable estimate until the dimension is resolved.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use selected_measure and program source row to choose required dimension. If unresolved, ask user/admin to select tons, horsepower, square feet, linear feet, unit count, kW, kWh, therms, gallons, or ports.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Program rows can use completely different units; wrong dimension invalidates the estimate.
inputMappings.notes: This is the canonical repair pattern for prescriptive tables with heterogeneous units.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Capture whether a required form, report, audit, or custom energy report is available. Link uploaded documents to quote/audit extraction where possible.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Missing documentation can prevent final incentive approval even if modeled dollars are correct.
inputMappings.notes: Use this to drive document-upload UI.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse numeric dollar inputs as dollars and convert to cents. If an invoice, quote, or receipt amount is available, prefer the document-derived amount for the applicable estimate stage. Use this field for cost-share caps when no more specific eligible or installed cost field exists.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Project-cost caps and percentage-of-cost incentives can be materially overstated or understated.
inputMappings.notes: Do not default silently. The testCaseDefault is synthetic $10,000 for QA only.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use program-defined eligible cost from itemized quote, invoice, or administrator-approved cost breakdown. If only total project cost is available, optionally copy project_cost_cents into this field for preliminary estimates and mark eligibility unverified.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Programs that reimburse only eligible costs may be overestimated if ineligible costs are included.
inputMappings.notes: Eligible cost is often narrower than total installed cost; require user confirmation or documentation.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use installed cost from quote or invoice, including equipment, labor, materials, permits, and installation-related charges when the program cap references installed cost.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Installed-cost caps, reimbursement ceilings, and not-to-exceed-cost rules can be wrong.
inputMappings.notes: Map camelCase and no-separator aliases through global normalization.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Installation, labor, and related upgrade cost
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse itemized labor, electrical, installation, panel, wiring, duct, and related upgrade line items from quote or invoice. Use only eligible line items when the program distinguishes eligible installation cost.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: EVSE, weatherization, HVAC, and related-upgrade incentives frequently cap or reimburse installation separately.
inputMappings.notes: When a raw key is a document rather than amount, store the document in invoice_document or quote_document and derive amount from extraction.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Equipment, material, EVSE, make-ready, and eligible non-labor cost
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Extract equipment, material, EVSE hardware, make-ready, development assistance, network, warranty, and infrastructure costs from itemized project documents. Retain subline classifications for program-specific caps.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Programs may reimburse hardware, make-ready, and network costs at different percentages or exclude some line items.
inputMappings.notes: Use more specific internal subfields when the program rule needs them, but expose a consolidated project-cost UI section.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use incremental efficient-measure cost over baseline when documented. If only total project cost is available, do not assume incremental cost equals total cost unless the program specifically allows it and the estimate is marked low confidence.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Custom incentives that cap at incremental cost can be substantially overstated.
inputMappings.notes: Prefer admin-approved or engineering workbook values for custom projects.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse receipt, marketplace checkout, proof of purchase, or invoice purchase price. Use MSRP only when the program explicitly uses MSRP or when purchase price is unavailable and the estimate is marked preliminary.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Purchase-price caps and reimbursement percentages may be wrong.
inputMappings.notes: Text purchase-price fields may include non-price proof-of-purchase language; parse only unambiguous amounts.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use final invoice or receipt amount for post-installation claim estimates. For point-of-sale incentives, capture confirmed instant rebate or distributor pass-through separately from gross project cost.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Final claim value, customer share, and pass-through compliance can be wrong.
inputMappings.notes: Do not confuse invoice amount with approved rebate amount.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Store uploaded documents and extracted structured values including vendor, line items, dates, costs, model numbers, installed quantities, and proof-of-payment status. Route ambiguous text to document review.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Missing documentation may cause an otherwise calculable incentive to appear eligible when claim proof is required.
inputMappings.notes: Use this mapping for document-like raw fields even when the observedValueType is text.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Store uploaded quote or application documents and extract line-item cost, eligible cost, equipment model, quantity, contractor identity, and proposed dates. Use quote for preapproval-stage estimates.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Preapproval estimates and cost-share calculations may be based on incomplete or non-final scope.
inputMappings.notes: Approved quote fields should preserve approval status and approver metadata when available.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse loan amount, financed amount, repayment term, monthly charge, and interest rate into structured financing fields. Treat market comparison and offered rate as separate values.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: On-bill repayment, loan, and customer-share estimates can be materially wrong.
inputMappings.notes: The testCaseDefault is synthetic and should not be used for user-facing financing estimates unless explicitly selected.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Capture required cost-share percentage, applicant share, approved project cost, match source, and non-federal match amount. Derive from program rules when fixed; otherwise require program/admin review.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Grant and competitive-program expected reimbursement may be wrong or noncompliant.
inputMappings.notes: Non-federal match text should not be coerced into dollars unless a clear amount is provided.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Distinguish approved award/rebate amounts from published table values. Approved values require administrator or award notice evidence; published table values should be sourced from current official sources.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: The model may double-count or replace calculated incentives with stale approved values.
inputMappings.notes: Use for review-only workflows, not as ordinary customer input.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Funding availability, program caps, and prior incentive history
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Check current program funding, per-customer annual caps, household or premise prior rebates, and one-rebate-per-home restrictions. Accept customer attestation for screening but require admin/source confirmation for final estimate.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Estimate may show funds or cap room that is unavailable.
inputMappings.notes: Funding status is time-sensitive and should not be cached as a durable package input.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Preapproval, reservation, or program approval status
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Map common approval, preapproval, prequalification, reservation, and pre-installation application statuses into a normalized enum. For fields ending in if_required or where_required, first check whether program rules require preapproval.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Many programs deny incentives if approval is required before purchase or installation.
inputMappings.notes: Use unknown as a visible placeholder; never assume preapproval is not required.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse as ISO date. Compare against purchase, installation, completion, and program reservation-expiration rules when applicable.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: An otherwise eligible project may be incorrectly treated as preapproved on time.
inputMappings.notes: Keep separate from application date and approval status.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse installation and completion dates into separate internal fields when distinguishable. For combined fields, use as the relevant deadline anchor only if program wording permits either installation or completion.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Application windows such as within 90 days, six months, or four weeks can be miscalculated.
inputMappings.notes: Do not infer completion date from invoice date unless no other date is available and confidence is lowered.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Purchase, lease, receipt, or invoice date
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse purchase, lease, preorder, receipt, and invoice dates separately when possible. Use invoice date for documentation deadlines and purchase date for eligibility windows when the program distinguishes them.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Deadline and preapproval-before-purchase checks may fail incorrectly.
inputMappings.notes: Fields about purchase or lease status may need an accompanying vehicle/equipment ownership status enum.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use application_date plus program deadline rules to derive within-90-days, within-six-months, or within-four-weeks compliance. If raw key is an attestation, store the attested status and still prefer date-based calculation when dates are available.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Timely filing requirements may be misrepresented.
inputMappings.notes: Application timing fields are eligibility gates, not incentive dollars.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Program, demand response, managed charging, or special enrollment status
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize enrollment status into active, pending, not_enrolled, ineligible, discontinued, or unknown and capture program name, start date, months enrolled, and anniversary when available.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Enrollment-dependent rebates and ongoing participation credits can be incorrectly shown.
inputMappings.notes: Special program names should remain as metadata because eligibility rules differ by program.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Income-qualified, environmental justice, disadvantaged community, or enhanced rebate status
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Capture claimed enhanced eligibility pathway and verification status. Geocode address or check program-specific lists only when permitted by the program and source data is current.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Enhanced rebates can be much larger than standard rebates, creating major estimate error.
inputMappings.notes: Do not infer income status from address alone without clear program methodology.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Customer class, sector, ownership, and site type
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize residential, commercial, industrial, agricultural, municipal, school, nonprofit, fleet, MDU, public-sector, and ownership/site categories while preserving program-specific labels.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Program eligibility, caps, and measure tables often differ by customer class or sector.
inputMappings.notes: This is a profile field, not a cost field.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Project site address, state, service territory, and jurisdiction
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Geocode address when provided; derive state, local jurisdiction, utility service territory, disadvantaged-community flags, and program territory eligibility from current official or maintained datasets.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: The model may surface the wrong utility program or apply the wrong location-specific cap.
inputMappings.notes: State-only inputs are insufficient for utility-territory eligibility.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Utility account, member utility, and participating utility confirmation
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use utility bill, account data, or official service territory matching to confirm utility, member status, meter/account type, and participating utility eligibility. Allow user selection for screening.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Wrong utility selection can invalidate the entire incentive estimate.
inputMappings.notes: Participating utility confirmation should be verified before final estimate.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Participating, approved, qualified, or licensed contractor/distributor status
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Capture contractor/distributor identity and user attestation; verify against program-approved contractor, trade ally, QCN, distributor, or license list where required.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Some programs require approved contractors or distributors and may reject otherwise eligible projects.
inputMappings.notes: Do not rely on contractor name string alone for final eligibility.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Qualified product, listing, certification, SKU, or eligible device status
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use model number, AHRI certificate, DLC or ENERGY STAR listing, program qualified-products list, SKU, or approved-device list to verify equipment qualification. User attestation can screen but should not finalize.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Incentive could be shown for non-qualifying equipment.
inputMappings.notes: Program-specific device lists are time-sensitive and may require source repair.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: AHRI certificate, cut sheet, Manual J, or equipment verification documentation
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Store uploaded certificates, cut sheets, and sizing documents. Extract AHRI number, matched system components, efficiency ratings, capacity, model numbers, and installation match status.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: HVAC and water-heating eligibility may be incorrectly approved or denied.
inputMappings.notes: AHRI match should be derived from certificate data where possible.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Equipment performance, baseline, dimensional, or operating metric
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Capture metrics with explicit units and retrofit context. Use typed subfields such as UEF, CFM, R-value, watts, annual hours, fan diameter, MBH, psig, ton-hours, controlled watts, demand class, or vehicle class.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Per-unit rates, eligibility thresholds, and savings calculations may be wrong.
inputMappings.notes: Avoid a single generic number field; these values have different units and validation rules.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Existing equipment, home conditions, and replacement context
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Capture baseline equipment type, age, fuel, central AC/heat pump connection, existing controls, replacement vs new construction status, and recycling/working-condition attestations.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Programs often distinguish early replacement, new construction, retrofit, recycling, and fuel-switching pathways.
inputMappings.notes: This group resolves many review-only fields into structured retrofit context.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Assessment, audit, recommendation, and verification status
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Track requested/completed status, audit result, recommended measures, recommendation grade, consultation timing, no-cost analysis eligibility, project completion docs, and post-installation verification.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Some incentives require an audit, assessment, recommendation, or verification before payment.
inputMappings.notes: Keep audit recommendations separate from selected retrofit scope.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Utility rate class, schedule, tariff, and rate enrollment
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Extract rate schedule/class/code from recent utility bill or account data; allow user selection for screening; verify EV, TOU, off-peak, gas, business, and nonresidential schedule eligibility against current tariff/program sources.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Rate-specific eligibility, EV charging rebates, and rate comparison values can be wrong.
inputMappings.notes: Observed numeric value types for rate schedule likely represent codes, not calculable dollar amounts.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Current rate, tariff credit, comparison rate, or energy price
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Retrieve current official rate, tariff credit, FiT price, comparison rate, on-peak/off-peak price, or administrator-confirmed rate. Store unit basis explicitly, such as cents_per_kwh, dollars_per_kw_month, dollars_per_mmbtu, or cents_per_mile.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Bill savings, tariff credits, and financing comparisons can be materially wrong.
inputMappings.notes: Do not use stale package numeric rates; current official source lookup is required.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Current official rate, rebate, tariff, or form table
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: At runtime, fetch or select the latest official program form/table and map selected measure to amount, rate, cap, and effective date. If inaccessible, flag program_source_repair_required.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: The incentive formula may use outdated amounts or missing rows.
inputMappings.notes: Applicants should not manually key official rate tables; they can select a measure or upload a form for review.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Utility bill, interval, metered, usage, and demand data
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse uploaded bills or interval data for account, meter, rate schedule, usage, demand, billing periods, demand charges, consumption thresholds, metering status, and baseline/proposed energy use when available.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Eligibility based on rate schedule, meter type, demand class, usage threshold, and measured savings may be wrong.
inputMappings.notes: Prefer utility data over manual user entry for billing and rate facts.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Estimated, documented, workbook, or custom project savings
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Parse savings by fuel and unit, including annual kWh, kW, therms, MMBtu, Mcf, MWh, O&M dollars, steam Mlbs, percentage above code, and greenhouse gas reduction. For custom projects, prefer approved workbook or engineering documentation over user-entered estimates.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Custom and performance-based incentives may be materially wrong.
inputMappings.notes: The synthetic test default is 10,000 annual kWh only when a test fixture requires calculability.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Verified or administrator-approved savings and baseline
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Use administrator-approved savings, verified first-year savings, approved baseline, metered savings, and demand reduction values for final calculations. Preserve baseline method and code baseline source.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Final custom incentives may be overstated and audit trail may be insufficient.
inputMappings.notes: Customer-entered estimated savings can inform a preliminary estimate but should not populate verified savings.

inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Store each metric with a required unit and basis, such as annual_mcf, annual_o_and_m_cents, annual_steam_mlbs, peak_kw, monthly_mwh, annual_mwh, off_peak_percent, or participation_percent.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Unit confusion can create order-of-magnitude errors.
inputMappings.notes: Do not coerce text savings values into a single generic savings field.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Load management, TOU, off-peak, curtailment, event, or participation compliance
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize participation, agreement, compliance, opt-out, event attendance, and off-peak charging data. Use program telemetry, monthly compliance files, utility account data, or user attestation depending on program requirements.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Ongoing bill credits, EV charging rebates, and participation-contingent incentives can be incorrectly estimated.
inputMappings.notes: Separate enrollment status from ongoing compliance history when data is available.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Grid connection, metering, interconnection, and operating profile
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Capture charging schedule, load shape, load calculation, meter/socket status, Wi-Fi or internet connectivity, interconnection approval, permission to operate/energize, and behind-the-meter confirmation.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: EV, solar-storage, and managed-load incentives can be ineligible or misestimated.
inputMappings.notes: Permission-to-operate raw numeric values should be treated as dates only if parseable; otherwise admin review.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Utility service status, new service requirement, and service start date
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Track active service, service fuel, new service requirements, turn-on/start date, primary residence usage, and service-account eligibility from bill/account evidence when possible.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Customer may be matched to programs requiring active service, primary residence, or a specific utility account.
inputMappings.notes: Service status is separate from customer sector and utility participation.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Competitive award probability or score placeholder
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Do not estimate expected value from a hidden probability. Use explicit user/admin scenario probability only for scenario modeling and label it non-source-backed unless award decision is known.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Expected grant values can be misleading for competitive or discretionary programs.
inputMappings.notes: The testCaseDefault 0.5 is synthetic for sensitivity testing only, not a recommended probability.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Award, procurement, selection, or notice status
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize award, procurement, RFP, round selection, and award notice statuses. If awarded or selected, capture official notice, award amount, eligible cost basis, match requirement, and grant agreement conditions.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Competitive grants may be shown as payable before selection or award notice.
inputMappings.notes: Award status should generally gate final grant estimates.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Program pathway, track, form, purchase channel, or installation path
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Normalize program path, track, selected form, purchase channel, marketplace path, direct-install path, contractor path, or application path. Preserve original labels because program pathways can alter caps and required documents.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: The model may apply the wrong rebate table, cap, or documentation rule.
inputMappings.notes: Program path is often a rule selector rather than a simple eligibility flag.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Organization, facility, sponsor, contact, and special site profile
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Capture organization, facility, sponsor, site contact, public access, MDU use, NEVI corridor, Tribal/Alaska Native entity, required forms, W-9 status, and anticipated revenue fields as structured profile or grant-application metadata.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Grant eligibility, site prioritization, and required documentation may be wrong.
inputMappings.notes: Some fields are applicant profile inputs; others are admin-review or program-specific grant scoring factors.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Permit, agreement, application, and compliance documentation status
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Track permit, application, program agreement, required form, confirmation, and completion documentation statuses. Route program-specific confirmations to admin review when not directly verifiable from user documents.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Program claims can be rejected for missing documentation even when dollar calculation is correct.
inputMappings.notes: Do not use generic text documentation fields as proof of eligibility without evidence.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Review-only eligibility, utility review, and screening status
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Hold program-review outcomes and screening statuses that should be determined by utility/program staff, verified source rules, or RetroFi admin review. Expose only prerequisite applicant questions in the main UI.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: User-entered review statuses can bypass eligibility gates incorrectly.
inputMappings.notes: Use this bucket for ambiguous review-only fields unless a more specific canonical field applies.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Current program status, open round, active tariff, or current notice
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Verify whether program round is open, current tariff is active, and current notice/table is valid as of researchedAt/runtime. If unavailable, block reliable estimate and flag source repair.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: Closed or changed programs may be shown as available.
inputMappings.notes: This is time-sensitive and should be maintained centrally.

inputMappings.canonicalLabel: Electrical panel, service, socket, and metering requirements
inputMappings.serverDerivationLogic: Capture whether panel upgrade, new service, socket, individual metering, or electrical work is required and link to eligible cost fields when costs are documented.
inputMappings.riskIfDefaultWrong: EVSE and electrification estimates can miss major cost components or eligibility requirements.
inputMappings.notes: Separate required status from cost amount.

retrofitQuantityOverrides.uiLabel: Number of fixtures or lamps to replace
retrofitQuantityOverrides.helperText: Enter the total number of eligible bulbs, lamps, fixtures, tubes, kits, or lighting control devices in the project. The prefilled 1 is only a placeholder.

retrofitQuantityOverrides.uiLabel: Number of charger ports or stations
retrofitQuantityOverrides.helperText: Use ports when the incentive is per port and stations when the incentive is per charger. Confirm whether a dual-port charger counts as one station or two ports.

retrofitQuantityOverrides.uiLabel: Number of HVAC systems or units
retrofitQuantityOverrides.helperText: Enter the number of eligible systems, outdoor units, furnaces, thermostats, zone sensors, or indoor heads, depending on the selected HVAC measure. Enter tonnage separately when required.
Enter how many eligible water heaters are being installed or replaced. Tank gallons and efficiency tier are separate fields.
Use this only when the program pays per measure. For insulation, air sealing, duct sealing, or window film that pays by area or cost, enter square feet or project cost instead.

retrofitQuantityOverrides.uiLabel: Number of motors, compressors, pumps, or controlled devices
retrofitQuantityOverrides.helperText: Enter the number of eligible devices. Horsepower, kW reduction, operating hours, or linear feet must be entered separately when the program rate uses those dimensions.
Enter the count of eligible windows or doors. If the program pays by area, also enter window square feet or total eligible square feet.

retrofitQuantityOverrides.uiLabel: Number of batteries, inverters, or storage systems
retrofitQuantityOverrides.helperText: Enter the number of eligible storage units or systems. Battery capacity in kWh and qualified model information must be entered separately.
Enter the actual number of eligible installed or replaced units for this measure. The prefilled 1 is only a placeholder until confirmed from a quote, invoice, worksheet, or user input.

retrofitQuantityOverrides.uiLabel: Number of fixtures, lamps, bulbs, controls, or lighting units to replace
retrofitQuantityOverrides.helperText: Use the actual count from the lighting worksheet, quote, invoice, or fixture schedule. The placeholder 1 is only for a preliminary test estimate.

retrofitQuantityOverrides.uiLabel: Number of eligible charger ports, connectors, stations, or chargers
retrofitQuantityOverrides.helperText: Many EV programs pay per port while others pay per charger or site. Confirm the program unit and count from the quote or award notice.

retrofitQuantityOverrides.uiLabel: Number of HVAC units, heat pumps, RTUs, thermostats, fans, motors, or eligible tons
retrofitQuantityOverrides.helperText: Use the unit count, tons, fan horsepower, MBH, or other program-specific unit from the AHRI certificate, quote, or equipment schedule.

retrofitQuantityOverrides.uiLabel: Number of water heaters, boilers, steam traps, fixtures, or eligible water-heating units
retrofitQuantityOverrides.helperText: Confirm the count and any capacity or efficiency metric, such as UEF, MBH, therm savings, or steam-trap pressure class.

retrofitQuantityOverrides.uiLabel: Number of weatherization units or eligible area
retrofitQuantityOverrides.helperText: Replace the placeholder with the actual quantity, such as square feet, linear feet, ducts sealed, windows treated, or measures installed. Use area-specific fields when the program pays per square foot.

retrofitQuantityOverrides.uiLabel: Number of motors, VFDs, fans, pumps, or controlled devices
retrofitQuantityOverrides.helperText: Confirm count plus horsepower, controlled watts, operating hours, or other program-specific unit from the quote or workbook.

retrofitQuantityOverrides.uiLabel: Number of windows, doors, skylights, or eligible openings
retrofitQuantityOverrides.helperText: Use the actual count and dimensions from the quote or invoice. The placeholder 1 may materially understate incentives.

retrofitQuantityOverrides.uiLabel: Number of systems, batteries, inverters, meters, or eligible storage units
retrofitQuantityOverrides.helperText: Confirm the program unit, such as system count, kW, kWh, inverter count, meter count, or approved interconnection/PTO status.
Replace the placeholder with the actual program unit from the quote, invoice, worksheet, or official measure table.

missingUiTodos.todo: Add a universal retrofit quantity confirmation step before final estimate whenever unit_count or a measure-specific count is missing, placeholder-filled, or derived from ambiguous legacy keys.
missingUiTodos.reason: A hidden default of 1 can materially understate or overstate incentive amounts.

missingUiTodos.todo: Implement dimension selector UI for ambiguous fields such as unit_count_or_tons, quantity_or_size, capacity_or_unit_count, unit_count_or_square_feet, size_or_savings, and multi-dimension prescriptive-table inputs.
missingUiTodos.reason: A single numeric value cannot be safely interpreted without knowing whether it means units, tons, square feet, linear feet, horsepower, kW, kWh, therms, gallons, or cost.

missingUiTodos.todo: Separate account identifiers from quantities in UI and backend validation.
missingUiTodos.reason: Several observed numeric fields contain account identifiers and must never drive per-unit incentive multiplication.

missingUiTodos.todo: Create quote/invoice extraction paths for line-item quantity, model number, equipment specs, cost, efficiency ratings, capacity, area, and unit dimensions.
missingUiTodos.reason: Quote or invoice values are higher confidence than placeholders and are often required for reliable final estimates.

missingUiTodos.todo: Add retrofit-family-specific helper labels and validation rules for lighting, EV charging, HVAC, water heating, weatherization, motors, windows/doors, and solar/storage.
missingUiTodos.reason: Generic unit count labels do not tell the user what should be counted.

missingUiTodos.todo: Add confidence downgrade logic when quantity, savings, cost, or dimension values come from synthetic test defaults or unresolved legacy mappings.
missingUiTodos.reason: Reliable incentive estimates require user-confirmed, quote-derived, utility-derived, or source-backed values.

missingUiTodos.todo: Add program-source repair workflow for measure tables whose applicable unit basis is not machine-readable.
missingUiTodos.reason: Some program rows use mixed units and cannot be safely resolved from raw key names alone.

missingUiTodos.todo: Add a visible retrofit quantity field to every per-unit incentive card, with retrofit-family-specific labels and no hidden default of 1.
missingUiTodos.reason: Quantity materially changes estimates for lighting, EV charging, HVAC, weatherization, motors, windows/doors, solar-storage, and many custom measures.

missingUiTodos.todo: Add itemized quote/invoice extraction and review UI for cost categories: total project cost, eligible cost, installed cost, installation/labor, equipment/material, make-ready, and incremental cost.
missingUiTodos.reason: Many incentives are capped by specific cost bases that cannot be reliably inferred from a single project_cost field.

missingUiTodos.todo: Add a preapproval/timing panel that captures application date, purchase date, installation/completion date, invoice date, preapproval status, and preapproval date separately.
missingUiTodos.reason: Combined date strings and hidden timing assumptions can break program deadline and preapproval-before-purchase rules.

missingUiTodos.todo: Add utility bill upload and rate selection flow with bill-derived utility, account, rate schedule, meter, usage, demand, and service status.
missingUiTodos.reason: Utility, rate class, meter type, and usage thresholds are eligibility-critical and should be verified from bills when possible.

missingUiTodos.todo: Move current rate tables, tariff credits, published rates, current program forms, funding availability, and program round-open fields into a source-maintained admin layer.
missingUiTodos.reason: These values are time-sensitive and should not be applicant-entered or cached as stable package defaults.

missingUiTodos.todo: Create an enhanced eligibility/profile module for income-qualified, DAC/EJC, customer sector, public-sector, school, nonprofit, MDU, Tribal/Alaska Native, and ownership/site-type statuses.
missingUiTodos.reason: Enhanced pathways often determine incentive tiers, caps, and program availability.

missingUiTodos.todo: Create an admin-only award workflow that separates award probability scenario testing from actual award selection or notice status.
missingUiTodos.reason: Competitive grants should not appear as deterministic incentives before award notice or administrator determination.

missingUiTodos.todo: Create a structured savings/workbook ingestion path for custom projects, with typed units and admin-approved verification states.
missingUiTodos.reason: Custom incentives depend on units such as kWh, kW, therms, Mcf, MWh, steam Mlbs, percentage savings, or approved baseline methodology.

missingUiTodos.todo: Add equipment-verification UI for AHRI certificates, ENERGY STAR/DLC listings, qualified products, SKUs, EVSE device lists, cut sheets, and program-approved submeter products.
missingUiTodos.reason: Many eligibility failures come from equipment not matching a qualified-products list or certificate.

missingUiTodos.todo: Add review-only routing for ambiguous fields that represent utility review, program screening, approved savings, approved baseline, or administrator-confirmed rates.
missingUiTodos.reason: Applicants should not be asked to self-certify administrator determinations as ordinary inputs.

questionsForRetroFi.question: Should the canonical primary quantity field be named unit_count or retrofit_quantity in the database, with the other retained as an alias?
Should EV charging estimates standardize on port_count as the preferred calculation quantity and derive station_count separately, or should both be first-class canonical fields?
Should RetroFi allow zero as a valid quantity for scenario testing and no-op estimates, or should final submitted estimates require at least one eligible unit?
What confidence threshold should block a final estimate: placeholder quantity only, ambiguous dimension only, or any user-entered value not supported by quote/invoice/source documentation?
Should quote/invoice extraction create line-item arrays for measures with multiple equipment types, capacities, or quantities rather than one scalar unit_count?
How should RetroFi handle programs that pay per dwelling unit, enrolled vehicle, account, or participant rather than per installed equipment unit?
Should account identifier fields be moved out of retrofit scope entirely into a separate eligibility/profile mapping prompt?
Should canonical cost fields store only cents, or should RetroFi preserve both original numeric value and normalized cents for auditability?
For combined raw fields such as purchase_or_installation_date, should the UI force users to split the value into separate purchase and installation dates before showing a reliable estimate?
Should award_probability be completely hidden from normal users and exposed only in admin/scenario tooling?
Should RetroFi maintain a central source-refresh service for current_official_rate_or_rebate_table and program_current_status, with package-level estimates blocked when a source is stale?
What internal subfield names should be standardized for non-count per-unit quantities such as square_feet, linear_feet, tons, kW, kWh, HP, MBH, CFM, controlled_watts, and steam_trap_count?
Should quote/invoice extraction be allowed to populate unit_count automatically, and should user confirmation still be required before final estimate?
How should RetroFi rank conflicting cost sources when a user-entered cost differs from a quote, paid invoice, and administrator-approved eligible cost?
Should enhanced eligibility statuses such as income-qualified, DAC, EJC, and public-benefit qualification require document upload, geocoding, self-attestation, or admin approval by default?
Should funding availability and prior rebate history block estimates entirely or display a warning with low confidence until confirmed?
Should all review-only canonical inputs be excluded from applicant-facing forms unless a program package explicitly requests an attestation?
